correctness.rationale: A bi-Lipschitz bijection between pointed metric spaces linearizes to a Banach-space isomorphism between their Lipschitz-free spaces. Each finite-dimensional normed ambient space is linearly isomorphic to Euclidean space, so every summand free space is isomorphic to one covered by Mason's Corollary 2 and has the Dunford--Pettis property. Mason's Lemma 12 gives permanence under countable ell_1-sums and complemented subspaces. Mason's Lemma 13, via Godefroy--Kalton lifting, gives failure of the Dunford--Pettis property for F(X) whenever separable X fails it. Therefore a complemented embedding of F(X) into the target sum is impossible. No computation or limiting experiment is used.

value.rationale: The result converts a family-specific nonisomorphism into a uniform structural obstruction for every separable source failing the Dunford--Pettis property. Allowing arbitrary metric summands with finite-dimensional bi-Lipschitz models makes the conclusion relevant to a broad class of finite-dimensional approximation and decomposition schemes, while the complemented-embedding form is strictly stronger than equality obstruction. The statement therefore identifies a natural limit on finite-dimensional ell_1 modeling of Lipschitz-free spaces rather than merely renaming the ell_p corollary.
